# agiter A client-agnostic harness for spec-driven agentic development: you write what you want, cheap models write the drafts, specs, tests and code, other models review them, and the harness keeps every step's input, version, review and decision in files you can read. The design and its reasons are in [docs/design-recap.md](docs/design-recap.md); what changed is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). Contents: [Install](#install) · [Start a new project](#start-a-new-project) · [Add agiter to an existing project](#add-agiter-to-an-existing-project) · [Models and agents](#models-and-agents) · [Describe the project](#describe-the-project) · [Workflows](#workflows) · [The stack](#the-stack-presets-blocks-packages) · [Commands](#commands) · [How a run works](#how-a-run-works) · [A run's files](#a-runs-files) · [Layout](#layout) ## The key idea: diverse points of view Every step of a run is done by separate agents, each starting with a fresh context: the author writes, the reviewer judges what was written against the input and the criteria, without the author's reasoning in view, so it has nothing to anchor on and no decision of its own to defend. A next round's author gets its version and the review, not its earlier train of thought. One long prompting session cannot give this: there a model judges its own work with the whole path to it still in context, like a person proofreading what he wrote a minute ago. Context diversity works with the same model too. Model diversity adds a second layer: a model's blind spots come from its training, and a fresh context does not remove them, a different model does. That is why every task has its own model files, one for its author and one for its reviewer: a cheap author and a stronger reviewer of another family make a good pair. ## Install Node.js 22.12 or later (Angular 22 needs 22.22.3), npm 11 or later recommended (npm 10 fails on some packages' peers, Vitest among them), git for isolated runs, and the CLI of at least one agent: [opencode](https://opencode.ai), Claude Code (`claude`) or Codex (`codex`). ```sh npm install -g @pavel.sommer/agiter agiter --help agiter --help # every command has its options and examples ``` Without a global install, `npx @pavel.sommer/agiter ` does the same. ## Start a new project `agiter new --preset ` makes a new project from a web preset: `agiter/` with the default configuration, the stack, `project.md`, the packages of the stack declared in `package.json`, and the least files that run: an entry page with an App component that shows `

Hello from

`. No sample app, no styles, no tests, no linters. ```sh mkdir shop && cd shop git init # optional; isolated runs need it agiter new # the templates and the presets that make a project agiter new --preset web-react-vite --dry-run # what it would write and run agiter new --preset web-react-vite ``` Nothing is installed yet: look at `package.json` (npm resolved the versions into it and into `package-lock.json`), then install and run: ```sh agiter install # npm install of what package.json declares npm run dev # http://localhost:5173 npm run typecheck npm run build ``` `agiter new --preset web-react-vite --install` does it in one go. The presets with a project: `web-vanilla-javascript`, `web-vanilla-typescript5`, `-6`, `-7` (`web-vanilla-typescript` is 6), `web-react-vite`, `web-react-express`, `web-react-fastify`, `web-react-next`, `web-vue-vite`, `web-vue-nuxt`, `web-svelte`, `web-svelte-kit`, `web-solidjs`, `web-angular`. With `web-react-express` and `web-react-fastify` there is also the API server: `npm run server` beside `npm run dev` (Vite sends `/api` to it; `GET /api/health` answers). `new` overwrites nothing: a file it would write that exists already stops it before anything is written (an existing `.gitignore` is kept). ## Add agiter to an existing project ```sh cd my-app agiter init # agiter/ with the default config, project.md from the base template agiter stack --detect # the stack from the project's files (package.json, *.csproj, …) agiter stack --show # what the models will get about the project ``` Or start the stack from a preset, which also declares its packages in `package.json` (through `npm install --package-lock-only`: nothing is installed, so you can look first): ```sh agiter init --preset web-vue-vite # agiter init --help lists every preset agiter install --check # package.json against the blocks: missing, misplaced, another major agiter install --dry-run # what would be installed, the npm commands agiter install # install it ``` `agiter init --preset --install` declares and installs at once. `init` makes no project files; that is `new`. The stack changes later with `agiter stack --add` and `--remove` ([The stack](#the-stack-presets-blocks-packages)). ## Models and agents `agiter init` copies the package's defaults into `agiter/config/`; change them there. `.agents.json` says how to call each agent CLI (`opencode`, `claude`, `codex`): its command, how it gets the model, what the reviewer may use, how its JSON output is read. Every agent you use is listed there; an entry may hold only the keys it changes, the rest comes from the package's entry of the same name. Mark an agent you use by subscription, so its calls cost 0 and their API price is kept for comparing: ```json { "opencode": {}, "claude": { "subscription": true }, "codex": { "subscription": true } } ``` A model file names the agent and its models, tried in order until one is available: ```json { "default": { "agent": "opencode", "models": ["openrouter/deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash"], "select": "availableFirst", "effort": "high", "timeoutMinutes": 30 } } ``` Which file a call uses, the first that exists: | Who | Files | | --- | --- | | the author of task X | `.models.X.json`, `.models.json` | | the reviewer of task X | `.models.X.review.json`, `.models.review.json`, `.models.json` | ```sh agiter models --list # which file each task's author and reviewer get ``` A cheap author with a reviewer of another family: `.models.json` with a flash model, `.models.review.json` with `claude`. Give `create-validation` a cheap model, `create-work` and `create-tests` a good coder. ## Describe the project `agiter/config/project.md` is what every task gets about your project beside the stack: structure, naming, scaffolding, your rules. `agiter init --preset` writes it with the parts its blocks need (the look as CSS custom properties for a browser app, unit tests, browser tests). Its section "Autonomous decisions" sets what the models may decide on their own; by default the effort goes into the functional core of the request, you decide what the user gets and how it behaves and every new dependency, and the look the input does not define is the author's. `agiter/checks.json` lists the checks the `checks` step runs after the work; every one must pass: ```json { "required": [ { "name": "typecheck", "command": "npm run typecheck", "timeoutSeconds": 300 }, { "name": "build", "command": "npm run build", "timeoutSeconds": 600 }, { "name": "test", "command": "npx --no-install vitest run", "timeoutSeconds": 600 } ] } ``` Their output is logged in `agiter/runs//steps/`, one log per check and attempt. ## Workflows The tasks (`agiter list tasks`): | Task | From | Makes | | --- | --- | --- | | `create-initiative` | an idea | an initiative | | `create-validation` | anything | what a working prototype still needs from the input | | `create-epic` | an initiative | one epic per functional area, and an overview | | `create-draft` | an epic or an idea | a draft | | `create-spec` | a draft or an idea | a spec with its acceptance criteria and its Scope | | `create-tests` | a spec | the tests (before the work, for test-first) | | `create-work` | a spec | the code | | `checks` | anything | the run of `agiter/checks.json` | | `create-profile` | a run | the analysis of a run (`--profile`, `agiter profile`) | A pipeline is a comma list: `task` is one round without review, `task:N` at most N rounds, each a version and its review. A pipeline file (`*.json`, `{ "steps": [...] }`) works too. ### From an initiative to epics ```sh agiter new initiative --name ocr-inbox # docs/-ocr-inbox.md, status Draft ``` Fill in its "Goal" (the rest is optional), list what you decided already under "Already decided", set `status: Active`, then: ```sh agiter run --input docs/2611151200-ocr-inbox.md --pipeline create-validation # what is still missing agiter run --input docs/2611151200-ocr-inbox.md --pipeline create-epic:2 --lang cs ``` `create-validation` is cheap and comes before the expensive steps; `create-validation,create-epic` does both on the same input. The epics are published as `docs/.epic.E1.md`, `E2`, … next to an overview. `--lang` sets the language of the output (without it, the language of the input); the headings the harness reads stay in English. ### From an epic or a request to code ```sh agiter run --input docs/2611151300-ocr-inbox.epic.E1.md --pipeline create-draft:3,create-spec:2,create-work:1,checks agiter run --text "Add a logout button to the header" --pipeline create-spec:2,create-work:1,checks ``` Give the work its review where you can (`create-work:1`): a work without one is done, not checked. A spec's section "Scope" (`- write:`, `- tests:`, `- protected:` paths) narrows what the work may change. `--includeFile ` (repeatable) gives a file to every model call of the run. Test-first: the tests are written from the spec, then protected from the work: ```sh agiter run --input docs/.spec.md --pipeline create-tests,create-work:1,checks ``` ### Decisions and open questions Where the input says nothing, the models decide and record it; at the end of the run the decisions are collected into `docs/.decisions.md`, yours first, each with an `Answer:` line. A run on a document an earlier run wrote gets that run's answered decisions by itself. A run is `blocked` when its last review blocked or the work met an open question (the input contradicts itself, or a criterion cannot be met as written). Its changes go aside as a patch; answer the question in the decisions report, then: ```sh agiter status # the last run: its steps, cost, what blocks it agiter continue # walks the steps again; nothing done is repeated ``` ### Accepting Done is not accepted. When a document and what was made from it are what you want: ```sh agiter accept docs/2611151200-ocr-inbox.md ``` It and every document of the runs on it, down the chain, get status `Accepted`, and nothing runs from them any more. ### Isolation: the checkout, a branch or a worktree By default a run works in the current checkout and commits nothing: you review the changes and commit them. In a git repository it can work apart: ```sh agiter run --isolation branch --input --pipeline create-spec:2,create-work:1,checks # branch agiter/, a commit per call agiter run --isolation worktree --input --pipeline create-spec:2,create-work:1,checks # agiter/.worktrees/; the project's node_modules found up the folders agiter finish --merge # back to the branch it started from, its branch merged (a done run) agiter finish # back without merging ``` ### Comparing models Change the models between runs without committing them (`agiter/config/.models*.json` and `.agents.json` are yours: a run never commits them), and run the same committed, Active input once per variant, each in its own worktree and named: ```sh agiter run --isolation worktree --name ocr-deepseek --input docs/2611151200-ocr-inbox.md --pipeline create-spec:2,create-work:1,checks # edit agiter/config/.models.json … agiter run --isolation worktree --name ocr-opus --input docs/2611151200-ocr-inbox.md --pipeline create-spec:2,create-work:1,checks agiter profile # each run's analysis cd agiter/.worktrees/ && npm run dev # try a variant by hand; git checkout agiter/ works too agiter finish --merge # the one you keep; agiter finish for the others ``` A run keeps the models of its start (`run.json`, `models`), so `agiter continue` goes on with them whatever you changed since. `--name` names the run and its branch and is part of its identity: an unfinished run of the same input, pipeline and name is resumed, another name is a new run. `--reset` throws the unfinished one away first (its records, documents, links in your input; with isolation its worktree and branch) and starts again. Without isolation, files the old run changed must be restored first (`git restore …`): a reset puts no code back. ### Looking at runs ```sh agiter status [run] # a run (the last one by default): steps, models, cost, limits agiter runs # every run, newest first agiter run --list login # the runs whose id, name or pipeline match agiter run --audit ... # record every executor call; agiter audit [run] shows them agiter run --profile ... # a model analyses the run when it ends: docs/.profile.md agiter profile [run] # the same for a finished run agiter run --delete --failed . # delete the failed runs (asks first) ``` `cost` is what a call was paid, `apiCost` its price by the API list. On a subscription the cost is 0; claude and codex calls record how much of the five-hour and weekly limits they used. ### Trying it without a model `plan` shows a run's steps; `simulate` runs it with a scripted fake model (outside a project in a new temporary one): ```sh agiter list tasks agiter plan --pipeline "create-draft:3,create-spec:2,create-work:1,checks" --text "Add a login form" agiter simulate --pipeline "create-draft:3,create-spec:2,create-work" --text "Add a login form" --script script.json agiter continue --root ``` The script says what the fake model returns, per task, role and attempt: ```json { "steps": { "create-draft#1/review": { "findings": [{ "text": "Problem unclear" }] }, "create-draft#2": { "responses": { "F-1": "fixed: Problem rewritten" } }, "create-work": { "changes": ["src/login.js"] } } } ``` ## The stack: presets, blocks, packages The stack is a selection of blocks in `agiter/config/.stack.json`. A block is one technology (a language, a runtime, a framework, a tool, a practice) in a version: what the models are told about it, its rules, paths, commands, and the packages it needs. A preset is a named selection that starts a stack (`init --preset`, `new --preset`); afterwards only the blocks count. ```sh agiter stack --list # every block, * in the selection agiter stack --add vitest tdd # add blocks; the blocks they require come with them agiter stack --add typescript@5 # a block in a version of its own agiter stack --remove tdd agiter stack --show worker # what one role gets (architect, drafter, author, worker, reviewer) ``` The presets: the web presets above, `web-aspnet-classic`, `web-aspnet-webforms`, `web-dotnet-sqlserver`, `database-mssql`, `database-postgresql`, `database-sqlite` and `far-luajit` (`agiter init --help` lists them with their blocks). The blocks default to the newest versions (Node.js 26, TypeScript 6, Vite 8, Vitest 5, SvelteKit 3, .NET 11, …); a block in another version is `agiter stack --add @`. The blocks' packages are a dependency map: each block lists what it needs and nothing more (React + Vite: `react`, `react-dom`, and as dev `typescript`, `@types/node`, `@types/react`, `@types/react-dom`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`, `vite`, `vitest`, `jsdom`, `playwright-core`). `agiter install` installs them through npm in the major of each block's version, never by editing `package.json`; a package already declared is left alone, and the ones you added yourself are yours. Your own packages for the map: `local.packages` in `.stack.json`. ```sh agiter install --dry-run # the packages and the npm commands agiter install # install what package.json lacks, or what it declares and node_modules lacks agiter install --lock-only # only declare them in package.json and package-lock.json agiter install --exact # exact versions instead of ^ ranges agiter install --check # exit 1 when something is missing, misplaced or in another major ``` npm 11.16 and later run a dependency's install scripts only when `package.json` allows them (`allowScripts`; npm 12 blocks the rest). The blocks name the long-trusted packages whose scripts are needed, also those their packages bring (Angular: `esbuild`, `@parcel/watcher`, `lmdb`, `msgpackr-extract`; Nuxt and Vite 6 or 7: `esbuild`; SQLite with better-sqlite3: `better-sqlite3`), and `agiter install` (and `init`, `new`) writes them into `allowScripts` before npm installs, so the scripts run at the install. For packages installed before, it runs `npm rebuild` of them. A package you denied (`false`) stays denied; your own entries: `local.allowScripts` in `.stack.json`. The models never install: the npm block tells them that `package.json` is yours and that a library it does not list is not available, so a work that needs one stops and asks you. Only npm so far; the .NET and LuaJIT blocks have no packages yet. ## Commands | Command | What it does | | --- | --- | | `agiter new --preset [--install] [--dry-run]` | a new project from a web preset: init, the least files that run, the packages declared (or installed) | | `agiter init [--preset ] [--install]` | make a folder an agiter project; with a preset, the stack and its packages declared | | `agiter install [--check \| --dry-run \| --lock-only] [--exact]` | the packages of the stack's blocks | | `agiter stack [--list \| --show [role] \| --add … \| --remove … \| --detect]` | the stack's blocks | | `agiter new [--name ] [--title ]` | a new document of yours from a template (initiative, epic) | | `agiter run --pipeline <steps> --input <file> \| --text <text>` | run a scenario (an unfinished run of the same scenario and `--name` is resumed; `--reset` starts it again) | | `agiter plan …`, `agiter simulate … --script <file>` | plan a scenario, run it with a fake model | | `agiter continue [run]` | walk a run's steps again from its files | | `agiter status [run]`, `agiter runs`, `agiter audit [run]` | look at runs | | `agiter profile [run]` | a model analyses a finished run | | `agiter finish [run] [--merge]` | end a branch or worktree run | | `agiter accept <file>` | accept a document and everything made from it | | `agiter models --list` | the model files of each task | | `agiter list tasks \| artifacts` | the definitions | | `agiter sidecar` | the API as JSON-RPC over stdio (for Far Manager) | Exit codes: 0 done (or planned), 1 blocked, failed or invalid, 2 usage. `--json` gives the result as JSON, `--root <dir>` names the project (by default the one the current folder is in). ## How a run works A run's pipeline is always given explicitly. Each step's author and reviewer are separate calls with fresh contexts; a next round's author gets the input, its version and the review. The harness puts into each model's prompt only what its task needs from the stack, then `project.md`, then the decisions made before it. A run that went through is `done`; one whose last review blocked, or whose work stopped on an open question, is `blocked`. A worker without a review decides what the input leaves open, but where the input contradicts itself or a criterion cannot be met as written it does not change the criterion: it names the contradiction under "Open questions", the run stops, its changes go aside as a patch, and the question waits in the decisions report. Tests an earlier `create-tests` wrote are protected from the work. A reviewer that changes a file fails its call (the file is put back); a profile's next model starts from the state before the failed one; a call past its timeout is killed with every process it started. The scope of a step is checked against what git sees. The owner's documents stay his: any file a run did not write is an input in the owner's own form (with a frontmatter `type` it runs only with status `Active`; without one it runs as it is); the pipeline decides what it is (`create-epic`: an initiative), and its frontmatter, status and structure are not checked. A run is named after the input file without its leading timestamp and stamped in local time (`yyMMddHHmmss`); the titles of the outputs are the models' own. A version is Active when another step follows and it has no review or its report is Done; otherwise Draft. A step takes only prose or an Active artifact whose latest report is not Block. The state of a run is its files: `agiter continue` walks the steps again and repeats nothing done. ## A run's files ```text agiter/docs/<run>/.<run>.md the input, copied as it is (never changed; a dot file) agiter/docs/<run>/.<run>.draft.1.md round 1 of create-draft:3 (a dot file) agiter/docs/<run>/.<run>.draft.1.report.md its review: Block or Done, cumulative (a dot file) agiter/docs/<run>/.<run>.draft.2.md round 2: input + draft.1 + its report agiter/docs/<run>/<run>.create-work.1.md the record of create-work docs/<run>.draft.md the result of a step, published docs/<run>.draft.report.md the step's last report, published docs/<run>.decisions.md the decisions report, for the owner to answer docs/<run>.epic.E1.md an epic of create-epic, published ... ``` Two kinds of output. Methodical artifacts (initiative, epic, draft, spec) are the documents a next run builds on: the result of each step (no review, or its report Done) is published to `docs/` (`agiter/config/.settings.json` `{ "docs": "<folder>" }` changes it), never over a file there, and agents never change them. Task records (`create-epic`, `create-work`, `create-tests`, `checks`) and the reports stay in `agiter/docs/<run>/` with every round; the versions of methodical artifacts there are dot files, so a client like Tolaria shows each document once (in `docs/`). Each document's frontmatter has the `model` that wrote it and the `cost` of that call. At the end of a run the file names in its documents become wikilinks (`[[name]]`, as Tolaria resolves them), and the frontmatter gets Tolaria's relationships: `belongs_to` and `related_to`. The owner's input file gets `has` (what runs made from it and keep), `model` (the models they used) and `cost` (their total, over the whole tree that grows from it). Frontmatter types are TitleCase and singular (`Spec`, `Epic`, `Report`, `Decision`); every task's record is `Pipeline`, its `task` tells which. ## Layout | Path | Content | | --- | --- | | `index.mjs` | the public API | | `bin/agiter.mjs` | the CLI on commander (`agiter --help`, `agiter <command> --help`) | | `sidecar.mjs` | JSON-RPC over stdio for long-lived clients (Far Manager) | | `src/` | the modules: definitions, pipelines, artifacts, engine, stack, packages, scaffolds, tools, log | | `defs/` | the package's artifact types, tasks, stack blocks, presets, scaffolds, templates, default config | | `test/` | `npm test` (node:test, no dependencies) | A project keeps everything in `agiter/`: `config/` (agents, models, stack, `project.md`, its own templates in `config/templates/<type>.md` and blocks in `config/blocks/`), `docs/<run>/` (the chain of each run), `runs/`, `logs/`, its own definitions (`artifacts/`, `tasks/`, merged over the package's) and `checks.json` (the required checks).

# Changelog What changed for users of agiter, newest first. The versions published to npm are the headings; the internal steps between them are listed under the release that brought them. The reasoning behind each change is in `docs/design-recap.md`, section 19 ("Added in …"). The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/); the package is alpha, so any minor version may change behaviour. ## [Unreleased] ### Breaking - 0.51.0: `run --new` is gone; `--reset` resets the unfinished run of the same scenario and name (its records, chain, published documents and links in your input; with isolation its worktree and branch) and starts a new run. `--name` is now part of a run's identity: the same input and pipeline under another name is a new run, so another name keeps both. - 0.51.0: `agiter init --preset ` also declares the stack's packages in `package.json` (`npm install --package-lock-only`: the versions resolved, nothing installed), so you can look at it first; `agiter install` then installs them, `agiter init --preset --install` does both at once. init makes no project files: that is `agiter new --preset`. `agiter install --lock-only` only declares; `agiter new --preset` declares the same way (`--install` installs). - 0.32.0: the models are per task, not per role. The author of a task uses `agiter/config/.models..json`, its reviewer `.models..review.json`, else `.models.review.json`, else `.models.json`. The old role files (`.models.architect.json`, …) still count until a run copies each to the files of its tasks; then delete them (`agiter models --list` says which). `agiter roles --list` is gone: use `agiter models --list`; the API's `roles` and `listRoles` became `models` and `listModels`. ### Added - 0.51.0: model variants without a commit: change `agiter/config/.models*.json` or `.agents.json` between runs; a run never commits them (a branch run leaves them your uncommitted changes), and it keeps the models of its start in `run.json`, so `agiter continue` goes on with the same ones. With `--isolation worktree --name ` each variant gets its branch `agiter/` and its worktree to profile and try. - 0.51.0: the blocks name the trusted packages whose install scripts must run (`allowScripts`: Angular's esbuild, @parcel/watcher, lmdb, msgpackr-extract; esbuild for Nuxt and Vite 6/7; better-sqlite3). `agiter install`, `init --preset` and `new --preset` write them into package.json's `allowScripts` before npm installs (npm 11.16+ and 12 block the others), and run `npm rebuild` for those installed before; `--check` reports what is not allowed yet. Your own: `local.allowScripts` in `.stack.json`; your denial (`false`) is kept. - 0.51.0: `agiter new --preset ` makes a new runnable project from a web preset: agiter init with the preset, an entry page with an App component (`

Hello from

`), the build configuration and `.gitignore`, the package.json scripts (`npm run dev`, `build`, `typecheck`) through `npm pkg set`, and the packages declared in package.json like `agiter init --preset` (`--install` installs them). Nothing else: no sample app, styles, tests or linters. It overwrites nothing; `--dry-run` shows what it would write and run; `agiter new` alone lists the templates and the presets; a call mixing a document and a project is a usage error. - 0.50.0: `agiter install` installs what the stack's blocks need and `package.json` lacks, through `npm install` (dev and runtime apart, the major of each block's version, no sample app or configuration); `--dry-run` shows the npm commands, `--check` compares `package.json` with the blocks (missing, in the other section, another major), `--exact` saves exact versions. A missing `package.json` is made minimal. The blocks carry the map as `packages` (purl, version, scope, when/unless); the project adds its own under `local.packages` in `agiter/config/.stack.json`. npm 11 is needed for some packages (vitest 4). - 0.49.0: the presets `web-vanilla-typescript5`, `-6` and `-7` (`web-vanilla-typescript` is the 6); `web-vanilla` is `web-vanilla-javascript`. The block `typescript` supports 5, and a fragment can hold for a block's version (`typescript@5`). - 0.48.0: the presets `web-solidjs`, `web-svelte` and `web-svelte-kit` with the blocks `solid`, `svelte` (Svelte 5 runes) and `sveltekit` (load functions, form actions, server-only code). - 0.47.0: the preset `database-postgresql` with the blocks `postgresql`, `postgresql-migrations` and `postgresql-entity-drafts` (a disposable test database from `TEST_DATABASE_URL`, migrations in transactions recorded in `schema_migrations`, short locks on large tables; the owner deploys). - 0.46.0: the preset `database-sqlite` with the blocks `sqlite`, `sqlite-migrations` and `sqlite-entity-drafts` (STRICT tables, foreign keys on, migrations by `PRAGMA user_version`, tests on a new database file). - 0.43.0: `agiter init` writes `agiter/config/project.md` from a template; `--preset ` (web-angular, web-react-next, web-react-vite, web-vue-vite, …) also sets the stack to the preset and adds the parts of project.md for its blocks (CSS custom properties, Vitest, Playwright Test); `agiter init --help` shows examples and every preset. - 0.42.0: codex's subscription limits after each call, read from its session files (`~/.codex/sessions`), shown like claude's. - 0.41.0: the agent `codex` (`codex exec --json`): the reviewer in a read-only sandbox, the author in workspace-write with network, `effort` as `model_reasoning_effort`; tokens are recorded, codex reports no price. - 0.39.0: a spec's section "Scope" (`- write:`, `- tests:`, `- protected:`): a work may change only its write paths (and the tests while no earlier step wrote them), never protected ones; tests written by an earlier create-tests are frozen for the work. # {{title}}

<!--
An epic: one functional area of a larger goal, delivered and checked on its own. Only
"Goal" is required. What you leave out, the run decides on its own and lists in its
decisions report for you to answer. Write in any language; keep the headings in English
(the harness reads them). Set status: Active to give the file to a run:
agiter run --input <this file> --pipeline create-draft,create-spec
-->

## Goal

<!-- What the user can do when the epic is done, and how you check it ("after dropping N files, the inbox shows N items within 1 s"). -->

## Scope

<!-- In: what the epic delivers. Out: what it leaves to other epics or to nobody. -->

## Depends on

<!-- Other epics, code or services that must exist first. -->

## Acceptance

<!-- The checks that say the epic is done: behaviours, edge cases, errors. -->

## Already decided

<!--
Decisions you have made already, one line each; every step follows them and does not ask again:
- Unsupported files are rejected with a notice. Why: the user must know why a file did not appear.
-->

# {{title}}

<!--
An initiative: the whole goal of a larger change. Only "Goal" is required; every other
section is optional. What you leave out, the run decides on its own and lists in its
decisions report for you to answer. Write in any language; keep the headings in English
(the harness reads them). Set status: Active to give the file to a run:
agiter run --input <this file> --pipeline create-epic
-->

## Goal

<!-- One or two sentences: what changes for the users. This is the functional core every step works towards. -->

## Users and scenarios

<!-- Who uses it and what they do, step by step: "the user drops a PDF into the inbox; the app queues it; ...". -->

## Must and must not

<!-- Hard rules of behaviour: formats, order (FIFO), limits, what is kept and for how long, what must never happen. -->

## Constraints

<!-- Platform, stack, libraries, services, existing code to build on. A dependency you do not name here is the owner's decision in the report. -->

## Look

<!-- Optional: only what matters to you (a layout to follow, a size, a brand). Left empty, the look is the author's. -->

## Out of scope

<!-- What the change does not do, so nobody adds it. -->

## Quality bar

<!-- A prototype to try an idea, or code to keep? Speed against polish, tests, accessibility, browsers. -->

## Already decided

<!--
Decisions you have made already, one line each; every step follows them and does not ask again:
- Documents are sorted newest first. Why: like Outlook.
-->

# {{title}}

<!--
The owner's conventions for this project: every model of every task gets this file, after the
project's stack (agiter/config/.stack.json). Where they differ from the stack, they win. Write
what the stack does not say: how this project is laid out, how things are named, what is
decided once for every run. Hints are HTML comments; delete them as you fill the sections.
-->

## Structure

<!-- Where things live: the folders, what goes where, what must not be touched. -->

## Naming

<!-- Names of files, components, functions, CSS classes, test files. -->

## Autonomous decisions

<!--
What the models may decide on their own beyond the harness's default (the functional core is
the owner's, the look the input does not define and the inner structure are the author's, a
new dependency is always the owner's). Tighten or loosen it here.
-->

---
when: [playwright-core]
order: 2
section: Testing
---
- Browser acceptance tests: Playwright Test (`@playwright/test`) with its own Chromium (`npx
  playwright install chromium`), specs in `test/e2e/*.spec.*`, run by `npm run test:e2e`; for
  these it takes the place of the stack's scripted playwright-core checks. Its configuration
  starts the dev server itself (`webServer`) on a port of its own (`E2E_PORT`, by default 5199,
  so the owner's dev server does not stand in its way) and stops it when the tests end; every
  test has its own browser context, so the owner's data in his browser is never touched.
- Adding these packages and the test scripts is decided; the first step that needs them adds
  them. Never start a dev server or a browser by hand and never leave one running.

---
when: [vitest]
order: 1
section: Testing
---
- Unit tests: Vitest (`npm test` runs `vitest run`). A module whose logic does not need the
  browser (a queue, a parser, a state machine) is tested here, with its storage and its
  libraries given as ports the test can replace (IndexedDB through `fake-indexeddb`).

---
when: [browser]
section: Autonomous decisions
---
- The look the input does not define is the author's. Anything that shapes the look and the
  user experience across the app (colours, spacing, font sizes, radii, shadows, focus and
  hover styles, transitions, breakpoints) is defined as a CSS custom property with a meaningful
  name (`--color-accent`, `--space-m`, `--focus-ring`), never as a literal value in a rule.
  Components use those variables; adding a new one is the author's decision, recorded once.
